working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: While Royal County Down sits atop every world ranking and commands a headline green fee to match, County Down as a whole offers one of the most rewarding links circuits in the UK and Ireland, with Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle making it worth far more than a single-course pilgrimage. The post treats all three as a coherent trip rather than treating RCD as the only reason to cross the Irish Sea.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (Championship Links), Newcastle, County Down: consistently ranked in the world's top five courses; sits between the Mourne Mountains and the Irish Sea in Murlough Nature Reserve; par 71, approx 7,186 yards; visitor days Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri/Sun (selected times only); advance booking essential and all groups must include at least one caddie; 2026 peak-season green fee £450 (Championship), £120 (Annesley Links); rising to £495 / £150 for 2027 season (confirmed on RCD's own enquiry page)
- Ardglass Golf Club: 18-hole clifftop links, founded 1896, expanded to 18 holes 1970; par 70, 6,268 yards; Castle Place, Ardglass, BT30 7TP; Irish Sea visible from every hole, comes into play on eight holes; clubhouse occupies a 15th-century fortified building (dates to 1405/recorded in sources as one of the oldest clubhouses in the world); roughly 30 minutes from Royal County Down at Newcastle, about 1 hour from Belfast; visitors welcome; green fee not confirmed with a reliable current figure (sources vary widely from ~£96 to £220 for 2025, treat as 'check before you go'); often paired with RCD on tour packages
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: 18-hole links, founded 1902; course redesigned/shaped by James Braid in 1934; par 70, 6,167–6,283 yards (varies by tee); situated on the Ards Peninsula, Cloughey, BT22 1JA; described as the most easterly 18-hole course in Ireland; nearest links to Belfast (approx 45 mins by road); visitors welcome every day; green fee listed at ~£40 by one guide (Albrecht/1golf.eu) — treat as approximate, verify directly; noted for value; recently recognised as 'Best Value Golf Experience in Ulster'; unique feature: 'The Dip' near the first tee, created during WWII airfield construction
- Getting there from GB: Cairnryan (Scotland) to Belfast with Stena Line, approx 2h 15 mins, up to 6 sailings/day; Cairnryan to Larne with P&O Ferries, approx 2 hours; Liverpool Birkenhead to Belfast with Stena Line, approx 8 hours overnight crossing with cabin option — suits Midlands/north England travellers; no passport control between GB and Northern Ireland; Belfast City Airport (George Best) about 50–65 mins from Newcastle; Belfast International also served from many UK airports
- Drive from Belfast to Newcastle (Royal County Down): approx 30–35 miles south, roughly 45–50 mins
- Ardglass is roughly 20–30 mins from Newcastle; Kirkistown Castle (Cloughey) is on the Ards Peninsula, approx 45 mins from Belfast
- Slieve Donard Resort and Spa, Downs Road, Newcastle, BT33 0AH: Victorian hotel directly adjacent to Royal County Down, borders beach on one side and the golf course on the other; part of Marine & Lawn Hotels & Resorts; 180 rooms; spa with pool, sauna, steam room; four dining options; rated 'Best Golf Hotel Northern Ireland' at World Golf Awards; informational mention only (no affiliate status confirmed)
- Green fee context: RCD Championship was ranked the most expensive course in GB&I in 2026 at £450, ahead of St Andrews Old Course (£355) and Muirfield (£395) — Turnberry is higher at £1,000 but in a different category; RCD fees have risen sharply in recent years (18% increase from 2024 to 2025 alone)
- Practical tip: visitor tee times at RCD are restricted; four-ball groups only; smaller groups may be paired with others; all green fee transactions must be in pounds sterling; full payment required at booking; non-refundable except for club-cancelled weather rounds
- Royal County Down founded 1889; Annesley Links underwent Mackenzie & Ebert redesign in 2015
